prompt: Create a profile settings panel for a language-learning app, Palabra. Fields: display name, native language, learning goal (dropdown), daily reminder time, and toggles for sound effects and streak emails. Then a 'Delete account' area and a 'Save' button. Deliver a single self-contained HTML file with inline CSS, system fonts only, and no external assets.
rubric: Related controls are grouped closer together than they are to unrelated ones.
Spacing follows a small consistent set of values.
Delete account is separated from the regular settings by more space or a boundary.
Labels sit closer to their own input than to the previous field.
Padding is comfortable rather than cramped, and the page isn't boxed into many nested borders.

prompt: Our admin dashboard sidebar looks cramped: menu items have 4px padding, group titles (Orders, Inventory, Reports) sit 4px above their items and 4px below the previous group's last item, and every item and group has a 1px border. What would you change?
rubric: Identifies that spacing between groups is not larger than spacing within groups.
Recommends increasing space between groups and shrinking or removing borders.
Suggests larger padding on items for legibility and tap targets.
Gives concrete values or a scale.

prompt: Improve this card list for a library app. HTML: three cards, each with a book title, an author line, a 2-line synopsis, and two buttons 'Reserve' and 'Details'. Currently every element has 16px margin all around, so the title and author have the same gap to each other as the synopsis and buttons, and all cards touch with 0 gap. Return an HTML file with inline CSS, system fonts, no external assets.
rubric: Title and author are visually grouped tighter than they are to the synopsis.
Buttons are separated from the text block by more space.
Cards have a gap between them that is larger than the internal gaps.
Padding is consistent and generous enough inside the cards.
Vertical rhythm is based on a few repeated values.

prompt: Why does everything on my page look 'boxed in' when I put each section in a bordered card with 16px padding? How else can I show that items belong together?
rubric: Explains that too many boxes create visual noise and compete.
Offers alternatives like whitespace, a rule, a subtle background tint, or alignment.
Says when a card is justified.
Gives concrete examples.

prompt: For a long list of 30 transaction rows in a banking app, which is better to separate the rows: a 1px line between each row, alternating background colors, or extra space between rows? The row has date, merchant and amount.
rubric: Picks one approach and explains the reason.
Considers density and the scanning needs of financial rows.
Discusses a downside of at least one alternative.
Offers specific values.

prompt: Build an invoice-summary sidebar for a freelancer tool: client name and address, invoice number and dates, a short list of three line items with amounts, a subtotal/tax/total block, and 'Send invoice' and 'Save draft' buttons. Deliver a single self-contained HTML file with inline CSS, system fonts only, and no external assets.
rubric: Client, invoice meta, line items and totals read as separate groups via spacing.
The totals block is separated from line items distinctly.
Buttons sit apart from the content with consistent spacing.
Internal gaps are consistently smaller than gaps between groups.
Padding is generous enough to not feel cramped.

prompt: Lay out a dense but readable control panel for a recording studio booking system: filters across the top (date, room, engineer), a day schedule list below with 10 time slots, and a side summary with the selected booking. One HTML file, inline CSS, system fonts, no external assets.
rubric: Spacing scale is consistent; the dense areas stay readable.
Filters are grouped distinctly from the schedule list.
Side summary is visually separated from the schedule without heavy borders.
Rows in the schedule have enough padding to scan.
Alignment of edges is consistent between regions.

prompt: A teammate's modal layout: title 20px, 16px below it a paragraph, 16px below that two stacked fields each separated by 16px, then 16px below a footer with Cancel and Confirm buttons right-aligned. The modal has 24px padding all around and a subtle shadow. Anything wrong?
rubric: Recognizes the modal is reasonably spaced and acceptable.
Does not require major changes.
If suggesting anything, offers at most a minor optional refinement (e.g. extra space before the footer).
Brief.

prompt: We have a form with three sections: Personal info (4 fields), Address (5 fields), Preferences (3 toggles). Should we divide the sections with cards, horizontal lines, or only extra space and headings?
rubric: Gives a clear recommendation.
Explains how the chosen method reduces visual clutter.
Describes spacing values or relationships between heading, fields and sections.
Considers when a different method would be better.

This empty dashboard cell looks lost:

inside a grid with 3 panels. Add enough styling to make it look balanced and give it consistent padding; keep it modest. One HTML file, inline CSS, no external assets.
rubric: Padding inside the panel is consistent and comfortable.
The heading-to-content gap is smaller than panel-to-panel gaps.
Styling is modest and doesn't add heavy borders or decorations.
The grid gutters are uniform.
